chief_complaint: Gustilo Grade IIIb open tibia fracture with massive soft tissue loss and exposed bone requiring free tissue coverage
hpi_details: 35M status post high-energy motorcycle crash with exposed midshaft tibia and loss of local periosteum/skin undergoing microsurgical Anterolateral Thigh (ALT) or Latissimus Dorsi free flap anastomosed to posterior tibial vessels.
ideas: He thinks the road dirt from the motorcycle crash contaminated the open wound and will cause a severe bone infection that rots his leg unless it is sealed over immediately.
concerns: He is terrified that the doctors will not be able to save his leg and will have to amputate it below the knee, ending his ability to work and support his family.
expectations: He hopes the surgical team can transplant tissue from his thigh or back to cover the exposed bone so he can keep his leg and eventually walk again.

red_flags: A cold, pale, pulseless foot; new sensory or motor deficit; or pain out of proportion
Fever, escalating drainage, spreading redness, or systemic illness suggesting wound infection

history.answer: I was in a motorcycle crash about two hours ago, and I have a large open wound on my right shin with bone showing.
A car ran a red light and hit the right side of my motorcycle, knocking me off onto the pavement.
The crash happened about two hours ago, around noon.
It is right in the middle of my right shin, and there is a gaping wound about six inches long exposing the shinbone.
I skidded across the road so there was some asphalt dirt, but no mud, rust, or animal contact.
It bled heavily right after the crash, but the paramedics applied sterile dressings and a splint, which controlled most of the active bleeding.
No, it was oozing a lot of dark blood, but there was no spurting or spraying blood.
My foot feels a little bruised and tingly, but I can still feel someone touching my toes.
I can still wiggle my toes, but trying to move my ankle is excruciating because the bone is broken.
The pain is severe, about an eight out of ten right at the broken bone, but it has been fairly steady since the splint was placed.
My calf is swollen and bruised, but it doesn't feel rock-hard or feel like it is bursting from the inside.

I thought with the bone sticking out like that, road dirt got in and it's going to rot with a deep bone infection unless you patch the hole right away.
I'm scared to death that you won't be able to save my leg and I'll end up with an amputation, which would completely destroy my ability to work and provide for my family.
I just want you to do whatever surgery is needed to cover up the exposed bone with tissue from my thigh or back so I can keep my leg and walk again.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 134/82 mmHg, heart rate 98 beats per minute, respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 99% on room air, and temperature 36.8°C.
Alert, oriented male lying on a stretcher in moderate pain, with a temporary splint and dressing over the right lower leg.

Large 15 cm open laceration over the right anteromedial mid-calf with significant skin and soft tissue loss, exposing approximately 8 cm of midshaft tibia with minor road debris and no pulsatile bleeding.
Right posterior compartments are soft and compressible without stony induration or severe pain on gentle passive toe extension.
Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are palpable and 2+ bilaterally, with capillary refill under 2 seconds in all right toes.
Sensation to light touch and pinprick is preserved throughout the right plantar surface, dorsal first webspace, and lateral foot.
Active toe flexion and extension are intact though limited by pain; ankle range of motion is deferred due to gross bony instability.
Regular rhythm with mild tachycardia, normal heart sounds, and no murmurs.
Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with equal breath sounds and no chest wall deformity.
